title: Lior and the Protocol
premise: Ulyana Oyelaran smuggles memories in sealed neural vials past orbital customs, and on the side maintains a beacon whose commissioning records have been erased from every archive. When the deep-space vessel Meridian returns with its crew biologically aged backward into childhood, Ulyana discovers her beacon is the receiver for their return signal — and that she inherited the post from a mother who helped launch them. The Meridian's crew carries a protocol requiring one half of humanity to wake from cryosleep before Earth's final transmission loop decays; the other half will be overwritten. Ulyana must choose between the faction that raised her and the child-crew who remember loving her in a future she never lived. In the end she broadcasts a third option through the beacon: a merged memory-archive that lets both halves wake as each other's found family, at the cost of her own stored self.
about_author: Kestrel Underhill is the pen name of a former radio astronomer who left observatory work to write fiction about signals nobody answers. They live above an old relay station and claim the static improves their prose.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Self
chapters.summary: Ulyana runs a memory shipment past orbital customs using forged grief manifests, establishing her world, her rules, and her loneliness. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: competent isolation — she trusts no one because every memory she carries belongs to someone else's love.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Maintaining her secret beacon, Ulyana finds maintenance logs signed in her mother's handwriting dated after her mother's death. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: uncanny inheritance — the first crack in her belief that she chose this life alone.

chapters.title: Meridian, Returning
chapters.summary: A ship older than any registry appears at the beacon and docks unbidden; its crew are children wearing adult rank insignia. Customs wants them seized; Ulyana hides them in her smuggling holds. POV: alternating Ulyana and the ship's captain, now age nine. Emotional beat: recognition without memory.

chapters.title: Children of the Long Dark
chapters.summary: The child-crew explains the Protocol: cryosleep archives hold half of humanity, and Earth's transmission loop ends in weeks, forcing a wake order. Their minds hold adult knowledge in failing containers. POV: Captain Iyo, aged nine. Emotional beat: terror of competence — knowing exactly what must be done and not being believed.

chapters.title: What My Mother Launched
chapters.summary: Decoding the beacon reveals Ulyana's mother co-designed the Meridian mission and hid the receiver here deliberately, naming Ulyana heir. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into awe — her whole marginal life was someone else's contingency plan.

chapters.title: The Wake Order Faction
chapters.summary: Orbital authorities, led by Ulyana's old fence Dagny, move to seize the Protocol and wake only loyalists. Ulyana must choose sides against the woman who taught her to survive. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: love against duty — loyalty tested by principle.

chapters.title: Memories as Evidence
chapters.summary: Ulyana opens her contraband vials publicly: the smuggled memories prove ordinary people's lives belong in the waking half too. The courtroom becomes a chorus of borrowed hearts. POV: Iyo. Emotional beat: contraband turned testimony — crime becomes compassion.

chapters.title: Loop Decay
chapters.summary: Earth's transmission loop begins collapsing early; factions scramble, the beacon overloads, and Dagny forces a binary choice with a countdown. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: desperation — every option costs someone everything.

chapters.title: The Third Signal
chapters.summary: At the climax, Ulyana realizes the beacon can broadcast a merged archive letting both halves wake entangled with each other's memories — but it requires a living mind as carrier. She volunteers hers. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship — writing herself into everyone.

chapters.title: Everyone Wakes Someone
chapters.summary: Both halves wake holding fragments of Ulyana; the child-captain, restored to adulthood, carries her clearest memory and tends the beacon in turn. Found family becomes literal inheritance. POV: Iyo, closing with Ulyana's voice in the loop. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into continuity — love outlasting the lover.
